convoLines.text: "What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on your first memory."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I wasn't a lifeguard. I was a pottery instructor. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
Vincent looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can I tell you something? I'm saving a candy bar for when things get better. I haven't told anyone."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on their secret."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on your plan here."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I dreamed Dominic was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I retie every loose knot in passing at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one. What's the worst that happens."

"It's my son, William. Asked if the taken ones were bad. I said no. He asked if they were boring. I did not answer. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Dominic owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I braid grass while listening to plans. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 7 days back. 'A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.'"
Vincent has an edge today — something curdled.
Their whole posture softens around you.
"I show up. That's my part."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Done."
"Good question." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Amelia shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
Amelia has an edge today — something curdled.
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about William? That's my read."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took me. Gauntlet — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening. It'll be fun, probably."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You told me about that kitchen — morning light, three years old. Have any other memories come back since?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
A beat. Then, as if shaking something off:
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took you — The Price, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Greenbrier Shoots today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that plant lesson."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Price. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one. Not that it matters."

"It's my best friend, Elijah. Was taken at the Scattering. We had plans. Stupid, small, beautiful plans. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? I mean it."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling tick? Vincent is pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The whole fire was arguing about tick last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Big' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
